dns.title: Reverse DNS names
dns.description: Resolve client and device IP addresses to names with PTR lookups. Use your gateway ({gateway}) or a DNS server such as Pi-hole or AdGuard that knows your DHCP leases. Several servers can be comma-separated; `host:port` is accepted.

data.dns_prefer: Prefer DNS names over hostnames reported by clients

manual_add.title: Add a device
manual_add.description: Add a wired device the map should always show, such as a server or NAS. Give an IP and/or MAC address. Leave the switch empty to locate it from the switch MAC table or ARP. Service discovery runs a quick TCP check of about 40 common service ports on this device only.

unifi.title: UniFi gateway
unifi.description: Read WAN status, ISP, WAN IP, the gateway's last speed test and UniFi's client names from your UniFi gateway ({gateway}). Use a local account with read-only (View Only) access. Leave the password blank to keep the saved one.

bandwidth.title: Bandwidth history
bandwidth.description: How the UniFi gateway's port traffic is recorded for the bandwidth graphs. Every reading is kept for the detailed history; after that, 1-minute averages are kept for the long history. Saved history is written to disk every few minutes and when Home Assistant stops.

data.rate_persist: Keep the history when Home Assistant restarts

nmap_missing.title: nmap is not installed
nmap_missing.description:
A full port scan was requested, but nmap isn't available to Home Assistant, so full scans use the built-in scanner instead. That still finds every open TCP port, but it's slower and identifies fewer services.

To add nmap:
- **Home Assistant OS / Supervised / Container:** nmap normally ships in the Home Assistant image. If it's missing, update Home Assistant; for a custom container, add `nmap` to the image (e.g. `apk add nmap`).
- **Home Assistant Core (Python venv):** install it with the system package manager, e.g. `sudo apt install nmap`, then restart Home Assistant.

This notice clears itself once nmap is found.
